mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has been on a recovering trend from -23.7 to -18.1 over three weeks before a small pullback to -19.9; the underlying improving trend momentum will reassert itself and push the 4-week average higher than the prior 4-week average.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -23.7 to -18.1 over three consecutive weeks before a one-week dip to -19.9
failure_condition: If the next 4-week mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the trailing 4-week mean despite the prior three-week improving trend, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility surged from -16.1 to +9.0 over four weeks, crossing into positive territory; this signals a seasonal substitution where households shift discretionary outdoor leisure time away from indoor retail and recreation venues, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above 0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS turned positive (9.0) at t-0w after being negative for the prior three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises alongside continued positive PARKS values over the next 4 weeks, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in WORKPLACES (from -19.1 to -11.3) and TRANSIT (from -14.1 to -9.3) in the most recent week indicates renewed commuting activity that generates incidental retail footfall near transit hubs and workplaces, raising RETAIL_REC over the next 2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved simultaneously in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks despite simultaneous WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improvement, the joint-commute mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 3.0 to 0.0 over four weeks, indicating households are spending progressively less time at home; in a reopening regime this behavioral shift frees time for discretionary retail and recreation trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell monotonically from 3.0 to 0.0 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean is lower than its trailing mean despite RESIDENTIAL remaining near or below zero, the behavioral-release mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls below -15 percent in any coming week, it would indicate a renewed restriction or precautionary withdrawal from public transport, which would curtail trips to retail and recreation venues and lower RETAIL_REC over the next 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 percent change from baseline in a given week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranged between -14.6 and -9.3 over the snapshot, approaching but not yet breaching -15
failure_condition: If TRANSIT breaches -15 but RETAIL_REC does not decline over the following 2 weeks, the policy-linked suppression hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-May seasonal warming in Madrid typically shifts discretionary time outdoors (reflected in rising PARKS) at the expense of indoor retail and recreation visits, so continued seasonal warming will keep RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean below its prior level even if other mobility categories recover.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose steadily each week from -16.1 to 9.0 over the snapshot period, consistent with seasonal warming
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean exceeds its trailing mean while PARKS continues rising, the seasonal substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained flat and mildly positive (3.4, -0.9, 3.4, 3.9) across all four weeks, indicating that essential-trip behavior is stable and not expanding; this stability implies no near-term behavioral spillover of increased mobility confidence into discretionary RETAIL_REC growth over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM values stayed within a narrow -0.9 to 3.9 band across the four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat, the essential-trip stagnation hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp one-week WORKPLACES dip to -19.1 followed by a rebound to -11.3, combined with RESIDENTIAL staying near zero, signals an unstable return-to-office pattern; this instability jointly interacts with transit usage to create inconsistent retail footfall, keeping RETAIL_REC's 2-week trajectory volatile and net lower than the trailing period.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week swing exceeds 7 points in either direction
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES swung from -11.1 to -19.1 to -11.3 across the last three weeks while RESIDENTIAL hovered near zero
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-2-week mean rises above the trailing mean despite continued WORKPLACES volatility exceeding 7 points weekly, the instability-suppression hypothesis is rejected.
